title: Cardinal Soglia to nuncio Viale Prelà, Rome 15 June 1848, printed in L'Italia del Popolo no. 40

documents.shelfmark: L'Italia del Popolo no. 40 (Milan, 30 Jun 1848), Roman broadsheet reprint (Tip. Puccinelli); Cipherbrain 13 Dec 2014

plaintext.source: Spada prints only the clear covering letter and a paraphrase; Il Labaro (7 Jul 1848) printed a guess.

transcription.source: Joe's transcription (blog comment #4) checked line by line against the scan
transcription.notes: Counted as single digits (955), not as groups: the text mixes the separator 5, two-digit groups and 8XXX codes. One dropped 4 restored on line 12.

system.summary: Two-digit 64-cell table of letters, homophones and syllables over digits {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,9}, 5 as word separator, 8XXX one-part alphabetical code for words, lone 1-4 as punctuation.
system.sibling_key: Same design as the 1814 Vienna nunciature cipher (Ramliden); not used as a key.
system.notes: Code stems combine with spelled endings; one print error (4 printed as 5).

prior_solution.where: Posted as unsolved on Cipherbrain 2014; no reading in Spada or Il Labaro

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Checked Joe's transcription against the scan; restored one digit.
5 as word separator (92 of 102 runs even); 8 never in second position of a dinome.
One-letter-per-group annealing in Italian, French, Latin.
Synthetic control solved exactly by the same annealer.
Injective letters+syllables nomenclator annealer produced circostanze, intendendosi, indirizzata.
Pinned those words and read the rest by hand; parsed 8XXX codes.
Alphabetical code order: linear rank model on 9 anchors checks the context readings of code words.
Content fits Lützow's departure, the nuncio at Innsbruck and Morichini (Chigi diary, DBI).

Open code groups 8093 8102 8131 8136 revisited for Lasry's quotation: interpolation anchored at the code start 8000 (fitted start 7996-8005) plus Colonia and the firm anchors narrows 8093 to ce- (cenno 8093-8097) and 8102 to ch-ci, 8131/8136 to early d; the sense words (volonta, mente, desiderio, ordine, comando, commissione, beneplacito; presa for 8136) are all excluded by position; corpus search found no phrase fitting both windows. Groups left open; d'assai for 8131 noted as a sense conjecture only.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 376 tokens, 75 types, it-modern order 4: reading -2.36 per letter; random keys -5.261 (z 5.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.653 (mean -2.721, z 5.2); annealer on the real text -2.251. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.36; polyphony 0.0; 11 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.251

outcome.method_basis: The letters-and-syllables nomenclator was broken by annealing on the printed 1848 cryptogram, with words pinned and the alphabetical 8XXX code read by hand; no earlier solution existed (Cipherbrain 2014 unsolved, Spada and Il Labaro give none).
outcome.notes: 11 code groups open, including the date of the earlier letter.
